answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a physical sonnet ledger of dated work attestations, shelved as a supervised relic in a reading room. A roaming inspector lands like a sparrow, unannounced, and quizzes the holder live against its own ledger; one operator cannot sit two quizzes at once. Each ledger needs its own reading-room slot and an archive fee in outside money that doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so every extra fake costs another ledger, another live human quiz, and twice the prior fee.
